correctness.rationale: Binary k-delicacy is equivalent to Hamming isolation at least k+1 in the fixed-length overlap-free language. Two enumerators in the original package agree on all words of lengths 1 to 14. Their full distance histograms imply no radius-2 isolation below length 13 and no radius-3 isolation below length 14. The complete extremizers are checked, including reversal/complement classes.

evidence: Przybocki, Theorem 1.4: ordinary delicate overlap-free binary words exist at every n>=7.

originality.rationale: The original scientific review compared the primary k-delicacy definition and open Question 5.1 with the exact minima L_2=13 and L_3=14; it found no prior statement of the two minima or their complete shortest-witness lists. This is a best-of-knowledge position, not proof that an unpublished census does not exist.
residual_risks: Unindexed computations or private notes may contain the same small thresholds.
